areas.summary: This area is the glue between OpenWhisper's logic and its UI. ApplicationController (1.5k lines) builds the recorder, the five executors, every feature runtime and the backend table. It owns the debounced engine reload, warm-up and meeting-lease state machine, the refusal gates (meeting, backup, setup, library), the Cancel fall-through, and the startup and shutdown order. It routes overlay states, status, transcripts and download progress, and handles Settings opening and staged building, meeting readiness, update hand-off with a hard-exit watchdog, and the restart prompt. Suggested port: a Qt-free core (state machine, gates, throttle, routing tables) under two QObject controllers, with the engine reached only through EngineWorker.

areas.summary: This area covers capture and everything that follows it. The PortAudio recorder records 44.1 kHz mono int16 from a ranked list of microphones, matches saved devices by name and host API, and moves to the next microphone if one is lost mid-recording. It ends the post-roll when the tail goes quiet, supports pause and cancel, journals audio to disk for crash recovery, and saves an atomic WAV with Explorer metadata. Around it sit the level meter, the live preview (re-decoded windows or native streaming), incremental decoding of long dictations, history playback, file preview and splitting, dictation languages, the dictation pipeline stages, Stats calculations, and two widgets (microphone check, capture delay). The port splits into a Qt-free core (PortAudio, FFmpeg, journal, stats math) and a Qt layer that sends decodes to EngineWorker.

areas.summary: Non-UI foundation services. areas.summary: This area is the meeting dashboard backend: a FastAPI/uvicorn server on its own thread that serves the prebuilt React bundle at /m/{token}, about 25 REST routes, and a /ws hub. The hub sends a hello snapshot, buffers patches that arrive during hello, fans out store patches (custom reports split onto host-only patches), tracks guest presence, and acknowledges client actions. Access uses a host and a guest capability token per meeting. There is also an archive adapter for past meetings. The recommended port keeps the React dashboard as a vendored static bundle, so the look matches for free, and rewrites only the server. That means a Qt-free core (auth, cursors, public projection, WS protocol, route handlers) under a Qt HttpServer/WebSockets or Beast transport, about 3k lines of C++. Contract replay against the Python server is the main parity check.

areas.summary: OpenWhisper ships through PyInstaller onedir freezes: an Inno Setup per-user installer plus a signed tar.xz update archive on Windows, deb and Arch packages on Linux, and a DMG on macOS. A transactional updater exe swaps directories with journal, health check and rollback. Components download with pinned URL and SHA-256, staged and swapped atomically. CI is 7 test jobs, 3 platform builds, then a verified draft upload. The C++ port drops PyInstaller, the Python wheel builders and the gpu-accel component, and replaces them with CMake install rules, Qt deploy scripts, a ported Inno script and shell packagers. The native updater is phased after a simpler setup-exe update. The doc includes a verified vcpkg and Qt dependency list.
